content:
Apple has major moves in October, with multiple major hardware and software products set to launch. Below are all the new Apple products worth looking forward to in October.

iPhone Duo will launch on October 23

iPhone Duo has been confirmed to officially reach users in October. Pre-orders will begin on October 16 (Friday), with the first batch of products arriving on October 23.

Supplies for Apple's first foldable model may be limited. However, the iPhone Duo will go on sale simultaneously in multiple countries, which could be a good sign for availability. Apple stated:

If supply of the iPhone Duo was expected to fall far short of market demand, Apple would not have launched this product in close to 100 countries and regions right from the start.

Read more: Apple unveils foldable phone iPhone Duo

Hardware rumours: new Mac, Home products and iPad mini

According to reports, Apple has quite a few new hardware products launching in October. New Mac, Home products, and an upgraded iPad mini are anticipated. Here are the details circulating:

  • MacBook Pro / Ultra with touchscreen: a brand-new high-end MacBook design featuring an OLED display, with more upgrades
  • M6 iMac: more powerful chip, with new colour options
  • M6 MacBook Pro: 14-inch base model MacBook Pro refresh
  • Brand-new Apple TV 4K: featuring A19 or A19 Pro chip, Siri AI and a new Siri Remote
  • HomePad: a brand-new home hub with built-in touchscreen
  • HomePod mini 2: more powerful chip, improved sound quality and other enhancements
  • iPad mini: featuring OLED display, powered by A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip

Two of these products stand out in particular: the first Mac with a touchscreen (possibly named MacBook Pro or Ultra), and the long-awaited home hub "HomePad". The rest are smaller updates to existing models.

Software releases: iOS 27.1, iOS 27.2 and more

Apple has confirmed that the iPhone Duo will run iOS 27.1 when it launches in October.

There is speculation that 27.1 will be a Duo-exclusive version. However, 27.1 may also be pushed to other iPhones, but it will only include bug fixes or security updates, with most new features designed for Apple's foldable phone.

Normally, iOS 27.1 would have more new features, but this time Apple has broken with convention — iOS 27.2 is already in testing and is also expected to launch in October. Therefore, iOS 27.2 is expected to be available to all iPhone users, while 27.1 is primarily for the iPhone Duo.

New features known so far for iOS 27.2 include:

  • "Profiles" feature in the Apple TV app arriving on iPhone and iPad
  • Group FaceTime calls add "dual-camera simultaneous shooting" feature
  • Siri AI will support multiple new languages
  • Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra and others may also see new features introduced

When iOS 27 launched, Apple confirmed that Siri AI "will add French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish next month". Since this language expansion is included in iOS 27.2, both 27.1 and 27.2 are expected to roll out in succession before the end of October.

The iOS 27.2 beta also includes a brand-new Health app with Apple Intelligence features, but this is expected to be pulled from the official release and reintroduced instead in iOS 27.3 later this year.

Read more: A look at all the new features coming to Apple TV in October

Among the new hardware and software releases in October, which one are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments section.
